stem.text: Let \( f(x) = -2\left(\sqrt[5]{x - 1}\right)^{7} - 1 \). Determine whether f is differentiable at \( x = 1 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is differentiable at \( x = 1 \) with \( f'(1) = 0 \), because the difference quotient approaches 0 from both sides.

worked_solution.text: f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), since \( f(1) = -1 \) and the root is continuous everywhere.
The difference quotient is \( \frac{f(1 + h) - f(1)}{h} = -2h^{\frac{2}{5}} \), and the exponent \( \frac{2}{5} \) is positive.
So the difference quotient approaches 0 from both sides, f is differentiable at \( x = 1 \), and \( f'(1) = 0 \). The tangent line there is horizontal.

options.label: f is differentiable at \( x = 1 \) with \( f'(1) = 0 \), because the difference quotient approaches 0 from both sides.
f is not differentiable at \( x = 1 \), because a sketch of the graph of f shows a sharp point at \( x = 1 \), where the root is 0.

options.label: f is not differentiable at \( x = 1 \), because \( f'(x) = - \frac{14}{5}\left(\sqrt[5]{x - 1}\right)^{2} \) is 0 there, so the tangent is vertical.
options.derivation: a zero derivative read as a vertical tangent instead of a horizontal one
